videos.title: Trump Won’t Rule Out ‘Mother of All Bombs’ on Iran, Taiwan Tightens Chip Curbs
videos.description:
Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh did nothing to dispel market expectations that the US central bank will hold interest rates steady when it meets at the end of the month. In a discussion in Bangkok at the International Monetary Fund’s annual meetings, Warsh made no remarks on monetary policy or his outlook for the US economy, apart from reiterating that the Fed will deliver price stability.

President Donald Trump declined to rule out using a weapon known as the “Mother of all Bombs” on Iran after the US midterms. Trump has previously ruled out striking Iran before the elections on November 3, which will decide control of Congress. Yet in an interview on Newsmax, he mused about possible attacks after the vote.

Taiwan is preparing to tighten export controls on AI chips to further align with US restrictions, according to a senior official in Taipei, joining a Trump administration clampdown on the smuggling of cutting-edge semiconductors to China. 

Today's guests: Ludovic Subran, Allianz Chief Investment Officer & Chief Economist; Elisabeth Braw, The Atlantic Council Senior Fellow; Dambisa Moyo, Versaca Investments Principal; Gustavo Pimenta​, Vale CEO 
--

videos.title: Why This Tiny Robot Could Fix Massive Sewer Failures | WSJ
videos.description:
In January, a collapsed sewer pipe outside Washington, D.C., spilled more than 240 million gallons of raw sewage into the Potomac River. It is likely the largest sewage spill in U.S. history, but just one of an estimated 75,000 across the country each year, according to the EPA.

As aging sewer networks struggle with growing populations and changing weather patterns, a team of engineers and professors in Europe is developing a robot designed to detect and potentially address problems before disaster strikes.

WSJ explains how the $9 million EU-funded PIPEON project is tackling the dark and perilous world beneath our streets.

videos.title: Why There’s An ‘Extremely Fierce’ Battle For TSMC's Limited Chip Manufacturing Capacity
videos.description:
Unstoppable demand for AI is leading to a capacity crunch on factory lines at the world's leading chip manufacturer, Taiwan Semiconductor. And it could put a chokehold on AI's ability to scale. Analysts tell CNBC that Nvidia, Apple, Broadcom, AMD and others are locked in an “extremely fierce” competition to get their GPUs, CPUs and custom AI chips made at TSMC. Capacity can’t come online fast enough, despite TSMC’s rush to build new fabs in Taiwan, Japan and Arizona, where has expanded investment to $265 billion. The strain has made one man at TSMC “the most popular person on the planet,” as chip start-ups and big name CEOs visit Taiwan to ask him for wafer allocation. It’s also created a rich opportunity for Intel, as customers look to the long-struggling foundry arm of the U.S. chip manufacturer for a second source.

videos.title: Private Investment for Jobs | Quick Take
videos.description:
How can private capital mobilization unlock investment, support businesses, and create more and better jobs in emerging markets and developing economies?

Watch this quick take from the World Bank Group Annual Meetings flagship event: Unlocking Investment Opportunities in Emerging Markets to Create Jobs. 

World Bank Group President Ajay Banga joined investors, regulators, development finance leaders, and private sector partners to explore how to mobilize private investment at scale. videos.description:
One week after a friendly summit between Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump, CNBC details an aggressive plot by China to infiltrate one of the United States’ most important institutions: the Federal Reserve. This explosive documentary delves into the incredible saga of a Chinese spy's effort to obtain secrets from the inner confines of the U.S.' top bank. It's a tale of sex, money, deceit and betrayal that put some of the country’s vital economic and financial secrets at risk. With exclusive access to new documents, audio, photos and text messages, CNBC's Senior Washington Correspondent Eamon Javers uncovers the story of former Fed economist John Rogers and a Chinese spy posing as an economics student who he befriended in 2013. “Inside Man” is a spy story at the heart of the competition for global economic dominance, posing the question of whether Rogers was a spy himself or an unwitting dupe.
